medium.title: The Ethanol Story Is Changing — Macro FX Angle: Crude Import Substitution
medium.summary:
While framed as a stock-picking article, it touches on a macro theme relevant to INR and India's current account dynamics. The article notes that India's ethanol blending program was originally conceived to reduce dependence on imported crude oil — a structural FX-positive initiative, as lower crude imports directly compress India's oil import bill, one of the largest drivers of the current account deficit (CAD). Any policy controversies or slowdown in ethanol adoption could, at the margin, imply higher crude import volumes, putting modest pressure on the INR. FX and macro-focused investors should monitor the trajectory of India's blending mandates as part of their broader CAD and INR structural view. The article does not provide specific policy updates, so its direct trading relevance is limited, but the thematic backdrop is worth noting.
